schemes.name: Small Business Innovation Research / Small Business Technology Transfer
schemes.ministry: Small Business Administration (coordinating 11 participating federal agencies)
schemes.tagline: Non-dilutive federal R&D funding — up to roughly $323,000 in Phase I and $2.15M in Phase II — with no equity given up.
schemes.whatIsThis: SBIR and STTR are federal programs that award competitive, non-dilutive funding to small businesses developing and commercializing new technology. Eleven federal agencies (including DoD, NASA, NIH, NSF, DOE, and USDA) run their own SBIR/STTR solicitations, each targeting technology areas relevant to that agency's mission.
schemes.objectives: The programs aim to stimulate technological innovation, use small businesses to meet federal R&D needs, and increase private-sector commercialization of federally funded research. Awards are structured in phases: Phase I funds feasibility and proof of concept; Phase II funds full R&D and prototype development; Phase III is commercialization, typically without further SBIR/STTR funding but sometimes through a follow-on federal contract.
eligibility: For-profit, US-owned and operated small business with 500 or fewer employees.
STTR additionally requires a formal collaboration with a US research institution (university, federally funded R&D center, or nonprofit research organization) performing at least 30% of the work.
Majority-owned by US citizens or permanent residents (with limited venture-capital-ownership exceptions under some agencies).
Principal investigator's primary employment must generally be with the small business at the time of award and during the project.
benefits: Phase I: awards up to roughly $323,090 (including modifications), typically 6-12 months.
Phase II: awards up to roughly $2,153,927 (including modifications), typically up to 24 months.
No equity or repayment required — funding is a federal award, not an investment or loan.
Awards above these caps are possible with SBA-approved waivers in select topic areas.
schemes.howToApply: Each of the 11 participating agencies posts its own SBIR/STTR solicitations on its own schedule. Search open topics and agency-specific solicitations at SBIR.gov, then apply directly through the awarding agency's portal.

schemes.name: NSF Innovation Corps
schemes.tagline: A hands-on customer-discovery training program for research teams, with up to $50,000 to test commercial viability before you build.
schemes.whatIsThis: NSF I-Corps trains researchers and early-stage teams to evaluate the commercial potential of technology coming out of academic or federally funded research, using a structured customer-discovery curriculum (100+ customer interviews) rather than a traditional business plan.
schemes.objectives: Reduce the time between promising lab research and a viable startup or licensed product by forcing teams to validate market need directly with potential customers before committing to a product direction. I-Corps also feeds later-stage federal programs like SBIR/STTR.
eligibility: National Teams: typically a PI, an entrepreneurial lead, and an experienced mentor.
Underlying research or technology usually has some federal-funding or university-research connection, though sites/programs vary in how strictly this is enforced.
Regional I-Corps Sites and Hubs (university-hosted, lower-dollar, often faster to access) are a common entry point before applying to the national program.
benefits: National Teams: up to $50,000 and a ~7-week cohort-based training curriculum.
I-Corps Sites: local, lower-dollar training (up to $100,000/year per site, distributed to individual teams in smaller amounts) with less red tape.
I-Corps Hubs: regional hub programming and access to a larger cohort/network.
Nearly 1,400 teams that completed I-Corps have gone on to raise a combined $3.16B in subsequent funding, per NSF.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through NSF's I-Corps solicitation for the National Teams program, or find a regional I-Corps Site/Hub at your university or nearest participating institution as a lower-barrier entry point.

schemes.name: Build to Scale Program
schemes.ministry: Economic Development Administration (US Dept. of Commerce)
schemes.tagline: Federal grants — historically tens of millions per year nationally — that fund regional organizations building the ecosystem around tech startups, not individual companies directly.
schemes.whatIsThis: Build to Scale (formerly the Regional Innovation Strategies i6 Challenge) funds regional economic-development organizations, universities, and nonprofits to run programs that grow high-growth, technology-based entrepreneurship in their region.
schemes.objectives: Authorized under the Stevenson-Wydler Technology Innovation Act, B2S runs national grant competitions across tiers — Venture Challenge (Ignite / Build / Scale, for entrepreneurship-support programs) and historically a Capital Challenge (early-stage capital access) — to build regional capacity rather than fund single companies.
eligibility: Applicants are typically economic development organizations, higher-education institutions, or nonprofits — not individual startups applying directly.
A founder benefits indirectly, by participating in an accelerator, venture program, or capital-access initiative run by a B2S grantee in their region.
Funding opportunities are announced annually and vary year to year — check the current Notice of Funding Opportunity on eda.gov.
benefits: Past cycles have awarded roughly $45-50M annually across dozens of grantee organizations nationally.
Grantee programs typically pass benefits to founders as accelerator cohorts, mentorship, or direct capital-access support rather than a direct company grant.
schemes.howToApply: Individual founders don't apply directly — instead, find whether a B2S-funded accelerator or venture program operates in your region via EDA's program page, and apply to that regional program.
schemes.howMuch: Indirect — via a regional grantee program

schemes.name: R&D Tax Credit — Payroll Tax Offset for Qualified Small Businesses
schemes.tagline: Pre-revenue and early-revenue startups can apply their federal R&D tax credit against payroll taxes — up to $500,000 a year, $2.5M over five years — instead of waiting for taxable income.
schemes.whatIsThis: The federal R&D tax credit (IRC Section 41) normally offsets income tax, which is useless to a company with no profit yet. Section 41(h) lets a "qualified small business" apply the credit against the employer share of payroll taxes instead, turning it into real, near-term cash.
schemes.objectives: Make the R&D credit usable by pre-profit startups doing genuine technical R&D (new or improved products, processes, software, formulas, or techniques), rather than only benefiting established profitable companies.
eligibility: Gross receipts under $5 million in the credit year.
No gross receipts for any of the 5 tax years before the credit year (in practice, a company generally younger than 5 years with revenue under $5M).
Must have qualified research expenses under the standard R&D credit rules (wages, supplies, and contract research tied to a process of experimentation).
benefits: Up to $500,000 per year of R&D credit applied against employer payroll taxes.
Up to $2.5 million total across 5 separate taxable years.
Remaining credit beyond the payroll offset can still be carried forward against future income tax.
schemes.howToApply: Calculate the R&D credit on Form 6765 and elect the payroll tax offset portion on that form; the credit is then claimed against payroll tax deposits via Form 8974 with the company's Form 941.

schemes.name: SBA 7(a) Loan Program
schemes.tagline: The SBA's flagship general-purpose loan guarantee — up to $5 million for working capital, equipment, real estate, or acquiring a business.
schemes.whatIsThis: The 7(a) program is SBA's primary vehicle for general small-business financing. SBA doesn't lend directly — it guarantees a portion of a loan made by a participating lender, which makes lenders willing to extend credit a startup likely couldn't get on comparable terms otherwise.
schemes.objectives: Improve small businesses' access to debt financing where private credit on reasonable terms isn't otherwise available, covering a broad range of business purposes.
eligibility: For-profit US business meeting SBA small-business size standards for its industry (NAICS code).
Demonstrated creditworthiness and reasonable ability to repay.
Cannot readily obtain comparable financing from non-federal, non-guaranteed private sources.
Actively operating (not a passive real-estate or investment vehicle) and outside SBA's excluded-industry list.
benefits: Loans up to $5 million.
Usable for working capital, equipment, real estate purchase/improvement, refinancing qualifying debt, or ownership changes.
SBA guarantee reduces lender risk, often improving approval odds and terms versus an unguaranteed loan.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through an SBA-participating lender, not SBA directly. Use SBA's Lender Match tool to find one, or work with your local SBA district office.

schemes.name: SBA 504 Loan Program
schemes.tagline: Long-term, fixed-rate financing (up to $5.5M) for buying real estate or major equipment — not working capital.
schemes.whatIsThis: The 504 program provides long-term, fixed-rate financing for major fixed assets through a three-party structure: a Certified Development Company (CDC), a senior lender, and the borrower, splitting the financing between them.
schemes.objectives: Help small businesses buy or build the fixed assets — buildings, land, or long-lived equipment (10+ year useful life) — that support business growth and job creation, on terms unavailable through conventional commercial financing alone.
eligibility: For-profit US business meeting SBA size standards.
Qualified management and a feasible business plan with demonstrated ability to repay.
Not eligible: working capital, inventory, real estate speculation, or passive investment.
benefits: Standard maximum $5 million; program ceiling $5.5 million for certain manufacturers and energy-efficiency projects.
10, 20, or 25-year fixed-rate terms, priced off 10-year Treasury rates plus roughly 3 percentage points.
Also covers qualified debt refinancing tied to fixed assets.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through a Certified Development Company (CDC) working alongside a participating lender — find a local CDC via SBA's lender directory.

schemes.name: SBA Microloan Program
schemes.tagline: Small loans (up to $50,000, averaging about $13,000) through nonprofit lenders for founders who don't need — or can't yet qualify for — a bank-scale loan.
schemes.whatIsThis: SBA channels funds to nonprofit, community-based intermediary lenders who then make small loans directly to startups and small businesses, with more flexible underwriting than a typical bank.
schemes.objectives: Reach very early-stage and underserved founders — including many who wouldn't qualify for conventional 7(a) financing — with smaller amounts of working capital and equipment financing.
eligibility: For-profit US business meeting SBA size standards.
Active operations and reasonable repayment ability, assessed by the intermediary lender (not SBA directly).
Cannot be used to pay existing debts or purchase real estate.
benefits: Loans up to $50,000; the average microloan is about $13,000.
Usable for working capital, inventory, supplies, furniture, fixtures, machinery, and equipment.
Repayment terms up to 7 years; rates typically 8-13% depending on the intermediary.
schemes.howToApply: Contact an SBA-approved microloan intermediary lender in your area — they make all credit decisions and set their own terms within SBA guidelines.

schemes.name: EXIM Working Capital Guarantee Program
schemes.ministry: Export-Import Bank of the United States
schemes.tagline: A 90% (up to 100% for underserved exporters) federal loan guarantee that helps exporters borrow more working capital against export orders.
schemes.whatIsThis: EXIM guarantees repayment on a working-capital loan a commercial lender makes to a US exporter, lowering the lender's risk and expanding how much the exporter can borrow against the same collateral.
schemes.objectives: Support US exporters — including small and early-revenue companies — who need financing to fulfill confirmed export orders but face limits on conventional working-capital credit.
eligibility: US-based business that exports (or plans to export) goods or services with at least some US content.
Underserved Markets Program (100% coverage): new to EXIM, total annual sales under $10 million, fewer than 100 employees, and otherwise qualifying as a small business under SBA size standards.
Standard program: 90% guarantee coverage for a broader range of exporters.
benefits: Funds materials, equipment, supplies, and labor needed to fulfill export orders.
Can back standby letters of credit used as bid, performance, or payment bonds.
Expands the borrowing base available against export-related collateral.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through an EXIM-approved lender, or contact EXIM directly for guidance on qualifying and choosing a lender.

schemes.name: MBDA Business Center Program
schemes.ministry: Minority Business Development Agency (US Dept. of Commerce)
schemes.tagline: Free technical assistance connecting minority-owned businesses to capital, contracts, and markets — MBDA doesn't lend or grant directly.
schemes.whatIsThis: MBDA is the only federal agency dedicated exclusively to the growth of minority business enterprises. Its Business Center Program funds a network of centers that provide business consulting, help preparing for financing, and help pursuing contracts.
schemes.objectives: Expand minority business enterprises' access to capital, markets, and contracts through direct technical assistance plus coordination with other public and private programs.
eligibility: Minority business enterprises (MBEs) generally — specific center services and eligibility criteria vary by location.
No revenue or size floor to get started; centers work with businesses at a range of stages.
benefits: Business consulting and technical assistance, generally at low or no cost through the Business Center network.
Help identifying and applying for capital, and pursuing federal, state, and private-sector contracts.
Note: MBDA does not provide grants or loans directly — it helps businesses access financing from other sources.
schemes.howToApply: Find and contact your nearest MBDA Business Center through MBDA's website.

schemes.name: USPTO Small & Micro Entity Fee Reductions
schemes.tagline: 60% off patent fees for small entities, 80% off for micro entities — a basic utility application drops from $1,600 to as little as $320.
schemes.whatIsThis: USPTO charges lower patent fees to small businesses (small entity status) and to individual inventors/very small companies with limited prior filings and income (micro entity status), reducing the cost of protecting a startup's IP.
schemes.objectives: Improve access to the patent system for solo inventors, startups, and underrepresented innovators, following the Unleashing American Innovators Act of 2022, which raised the small-entity discount from 50% to 60% and the micro-entity discount from 75% to 80%.
eligibility: Small entity: generally fewer than 500 employees (including affiliates), and patent rights not assigned to a non-small entity.
Micro entity (37 CFR 1.29): must also meet income limits and have filed on a limited number of prior applications — check current USPTO thresholds before relying on this status.
benefits: Small entity: 60% off standard patent fees (e.g., $640 vs. $1,600 for a basic utility filing fee).
Micro entity: 80% off standard fees (e.g., $320 for the same filing).
Savings compound across filing, issuance, and maintenance fees over a patent's life.
schemes.howToApply: Claim small or micro entity status directly on your patent application filing (via USPTO's Patent Center) — no separate application is required, but entity-status requirements must be met and certified accurately.

schemes.name: Opportunity Zones
schemes.tagline: A tax-deferral and tax-free-growth incentive for investors who put capital gains into a startup or project located in a designated low-income census tract.
schemes.whatIsThis: Opportunity Zones let investors defer tax on capital gains by reinvesting them into a Qualified Opportunity Fund (QOF), which then invests in qualifying businesses, real estate, or infrastructure inside a federally designated Opportunity Zone. Originally created by the 2017 Tax Cuts and Jobs Act, the program was made permanent by the One Big Beautiful Bill Act.
schemes.objectives: Direct private investment capital into economically distressed communities by making that investment more tax-advantaged than an equivalent investment elsewhere.
eligibility: A startup benefits by being physically located and substantially operating within a designated Opportunity Zone census tract.
Investors must reinvest realized capital gains into a Qualified Opportunity Fund within 180 days of the gain-generating sale.
The QOF must meet ongoing asset and operating tests to remain a qualifying investment vehicle.
benefits: Investors defer tax on the original reinvested capital gain.
If the QOF investment is held at least 10 years, appreciation on that investment becomes entirely tax-free.
Can make a startup materially more attractive to investors already sitting on unrealized gains, purely because of where the company is located.
schemes.howToApply: Not something a startup "applies" for directly — check whether your business location is inside a designated zone, and structure investment through a Qualified Opportunity Fund with tax counsel.

schemes.name: Qualified Small Business Stock Exclusion (Section 1202)
schemes.tagline: Founders and early investors in a qualifying C-corp can exclude up to the greater of $15M or 10x their basis from capital gains tax — with 100% exclusion after a 5-year hold on stock issued after July 4, 2025.
schemes.whatIsThis: Section 1202 of the tax code lets noncorporate taxpayers exclude some or all capital gain from selling Qualified Small Business Stock, provided the issuing company and the stock meet specific requirements. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (signed July 4, 2025) expanded these benefits significantly for stock issued after that date.
schemes.objectives: Encourage investment in small, active US C-corporations by substantially reducing or eliminating the tax cost of a successful exit for founders and early shareholders.
eligibility: Stock must be issued directly by a domestic C-corporation with gross assets under a statutory cap ($75M under OBBBA for post-7/4/2025 stock, up from $50M previously) at issuance.

Company must be an active qualified trade or business — excluded categories include businesses whose principal asset is an employee's reputation/skill (many professional services), plus banking, insurance, financing, leasing, investing, farming, and hospitality.
Stock must be acquired at original issuance (not purchased secondhand) and held by the taxpayer.
benefits: For stock issued after July 4, 2025: a tiered schedule — 50% exclusion at a 3-year hold, 75% at 4 years, 100% at 5 years.
Gain cap: the greater of $15 million (indexed for inflation) or 10x the shareholder's basis, for post-7/4/2025 stock.
Stock issued on or before July 4, 2025 keeps the prior rule: a strict 5-year hold for any exclusion, capped at $10 million or 10x basis, with no partial exclusion before 5 years.
schemes.howToApply: Not an application — confirm QSBS eligibility with tax counsel at formation and again before any sale, since eligibility depends on facts fixed at issuance (entity type, gross assets, business activity).

schemes.name: Federal Small Business Contracting Set-Asides
schemes.tagline: 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB/EDWOSB and SDVOSB certifications restrict a slice of federal contracting dollars to qualifying small businesses — including sole-source awards up to $4.5-7M.
schemes.whatIsThis: A federal set-aside restricts a contract, or part of one, to a specific category of certified small business rather than opening it to full and open competition. The federal government targets 23% of prime contract dollars to small businesses overall, with sub-goals for each certification category.
schemes.objectives: Give small, disadvantaged, minority-, women-, veteran-, and HUBZone-located businesses a realistic path into a federal contracting market that would otherwise be dominated by large, established contractors.
eligibility: 8(a) Business Development: small business owned by a socially and economically disadvantaged individual; a 9-year program with defined revenue/net-worth caps.
HUBZone: principal office and a required share of employees located in a Historically Underutilized Business Zone.
WOSB/EDWOSB: at least 51% owned and controlled by women (economically disadvantaged for EDWOSB).
SDVOSB: at least 51% owned and controlled by a service-disabled veteran.
All require an active SAM.gov registration with a Unique Entity Identifier; multiple certifications can be held simultaneously (e.g., 8(a) + SDVOSB).
benefits: 8(a): sole-source contracts up to $7M (manufacturing) or $4.5M (services), plus competitive 8(a) set-asides and Mentor-Protégé program access.
HUBZone: a 10% price-evaluation preference in full-and-open competitions, plus sole-source contracts up to $4.5M.
WOSB/SDVOSB: dedicated set-aside competitions restricted to certified firms in relevant industries.
schemes.howToApply: Register on SAM.gov first, then apply for the relevant certification(s) through SBA's certification portal — certification is free; be cautious of paid "certification services."

schemes.name: APEX Accelerators (formerly PTAC)
schemes.ministry: Department of Defense, Office of Small Business Programs
schemes.tagline: Free, one-on-one help winning government contracts — bid reviews, certifications, and required registrations — from a network of 96+ centers nationwide.
schemes.whatIsThis: APEX Accelerators (renamed from Procurement Technical Assistance Centers in FY2023) provide free technical assistance to businesses pursuing federal, state, and local government contracts, and subcontracts with government prime contractors.
schemes.objectives: Build resilient US supply chains by helping a broad range of businesses — not just defense contractors — successfully compete for and perform on government contracts, congressionally authorized since 1986.
eligibility: Any US business interested in government contracting, at any stage of readiness.
No revenue or certification prerequisites to get started — many clients use an APEX Accelerator to prepare for SAM.gov registration and set-aside certifications in the first place.
benefits: Bid and proposal reviews, marketing assistance, and contract-performance support.
Help navigating small-business certifications (8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB) and required registrations.
Procurement training classes and seminars, generally at no cost.
schemes.howToApply: Find your local APEX Accelerator (there are 96+ nationwide, often hosted by universities or state economic-development agencies) and contact them directly — services are free.

schemes.name: Small Business Investment Company Program
schemes.tagline: SBA licenses and backs private investment funds that then invest equity or debt into startups and small businesses — a government-leveraged path into venture-style capital.
schemes.whatIsThis: Created in 1958, the SBIC program doesn't fund startups directly. Instead, SBA licenses privately owned and managed investment funds (SBICs) and lets them borrow government-guaranteed debt on top of the private capital they raise, then deploy that combined capital as equity or debt into small businesses.
schemes.objectives: Stimulate and supplement the flow of private equity and long-term loan capital that small businesses need for financing, growth, expansion, and modernization — reaching companies that wouldn't otherwise attract enough private venture capital alone.
eligibility: A startup doesn't apply to SBA directly — it raises from a licensed SBIC fund the same way it would from any VC or private debt fund.
Must meet SBA small-business size standards to receive SBIC-sourced capital.
Find a licensed SBIC through SBA's public list of SBA-licensed fund managers.
benefits: For every $1 an SBIC fund raises from private investors, SBA can commit up to $2 of guaranteed debt (leverage), subject to a per-fund cap.
In FY2025 the program reached $53 billion in combined private capital and SBA leverage nationally.
SBICs can invest as equity, debt, or a mix, depending on the fund's strategy.
schemes.howToApply: Identify and pitch a licensed SBIC fund directly, the same way you would approach any venture or private-debt investor — SBA's site lists licensed SBICs by focus area.
schemes.maxFunding: Fund-dependent (SBA leverage up to $175M per fund)

schemes.name: DOE Office of Small Business Programs
schemes.tagline: DOE's dedicated office for helping small businesses win contracts and subcontracts across the Department's labs and programs.
schemes.whatIsThis: The Office of Small Business Programs (formerly the Office of Small and Disadvantaged Business Utilization) works to maximize the share of DOE contracting dollars that go to small businesses, including those certified 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, and SDVOSB.
schemes.objectives: Make it easier for small businesses to do business with DOE, connect them productively with internal DOE stakeholders and national labs, and improve DOE's small-business and socio-economic contracting performance.
eligibility: Any small business under SBA size standards interested in DOE contracting or subcontracting opportunities.
Relevant socio-economic certifications (8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB) strengthen set-aside eligibility but aren't required to engage with the office.
benefits: Direct guidance navigating DOE and national-lab procurement.
Connections to DOE prime contractors seeking small-business subcontractors.
A path into DOE's broader small-business contracting goals across its labs and program offices.
limitations: This is a contracting-assistance office, not a grant or loan program — it doesn't provide direct funding.
schemes.howToApply: Contact DOE's Office of Small Business Programs directly and register in SAM.gov to be discoverable for DOE contracting opportunities.

links.label: DOE — Office of Small Business Programs

schemes.name: Rural Business Development Grants
schemes.ministry: US Department of Agriculture, Rural Development
schemes.tagline: USDA grants that fund local and regional organizations supporting small, emerging rural businesses — reaching founders indirectly through those intermediaries.
schemes.whatIsThis: Rural Business Development Grants fund technical assistance, training, and infrastructure that help small and emerging private businesses in rural areas grow — similar in structure to EDA's Build to Scale, the grant goes to a supporting organization, not straight to a startup.
schemes.objectives: Promote economic development and job creation in rural areas by strengthening the organizations and infrastructure that support small rural businesses, split across Enterprise Grants (broader business support) and Opportunity Grants (economically distressed and underserved areas).
eligibility: Grantees are public bodies, federally recognized tribes, or nonprofits serving rural areas — not individual for-profit businesses.
A rural startup benefits indirectly, through business counseling, training, or revolving-loan funds a grantee organization runs.
Target businesses for the underlying support are generally rural, for-profit, with fewer than 50 employees and under $1 million in gross annual revenue.
benefits: Funds project planning, business counseling, and technical assistance for rural entrepreneurs.
Can capitalize revolving loan funds that rural startups later borrow from.
Can fund land, buildings, and infrastructure supporting rural business development.
limitations: Not a direct-to-startup grant — a rural founder needs to find and work with a funded intermediary rather than applying to USDA directly.
schemes.howToApply: Individual founders should contact their state USDA Rural Development office to find an active RBDG-funded organization offering support in their area.

links.label: USDA Rural Development — Rural Business Development Grants

schemes.howMuch: Indirect — via a funded rural intermediary

schemes.name: Manufacturing Extension Partnership
schemes.ministry: National Institute of Standards and Technology (NIST)
schemes.tagline: Free-to-low-cost technical assistance from a nationwide network of 51 MEP Centers helping small manufacturers adopt new technology and improve production.
schemes.whatIsThis: MEP is a network of centers in all 50 states and Puerto Rico that helps small and medium-sized manufacturers (500 or fewer employees) improve production processes, adopt new technology, and bring new products to market. Since 1988 it has worked with more than 86,000 manufacturers.
schemes.objectives: Strengthen US manufacturing competitiveness by pairing small manufacturers with trusted local advisors — over 1,450 of them across more than 430 service locations — combining federal funding with matched state contributions.
eligibility: US-based small or medium-sized manufacturer (typically 500 or fewer employees).
Services are client-fee-based for larger firms but often subsidized or free for smaller ones — check with your local Center.
benefits: Hands-on help with process improvement, technology adoption, workforce training, and supply-chain upgrades.
Access to a trusted local advisor network rather than a generic hotline.
Historic impact: $96.4B in sales impact and nearly 800,000 jobs supported since 1988.
schemes.howToApply: Find and contact your state's MEP Center directly through the national NIST MEP site.
schemes.maxFunding: Technical assistance (fee varies by firm size)
schemes.howMuch: Often free or low-cost for small manufacturers

schemes.name: Advanced Research Projects Agency-Energy
schemes.tagline: DOE's DARPA-style program funding high-risk, high-reward energy technology too early for private investment — average award $2-3M over several years.
schemes.whatIsThis: ARPA-E funds transformational energy technologies at a stage before they're ready for private-sector investment, working with academia, national labs, startups, and small businesses.
schemes.objectives: Accelerate energy innovations that improve US energy security, affordability, and sustainability, established by the America COMPETES Act of 2007.
eligibility: Open to startups, small businesses, universities, and national labs proposing high-potential, early-stage energy technology.
Apply through specific ARPA-E funding opportunity announcements (FOAs), not a rolling general application.
benefits: Average award of $2-3 million per project over several years.
$3.27B provided to over 1,415 projects since 2009 through September 2022.
200+ funded projects have attracted over $11B in private follow-on funding; 131 companies formed from ARPA-E projects.
schemes.howToApply: Monitor and apply through ARPA-E eXCHANGE for open funding opportunity announcements in your technology area.

schemes.name: Rural Energy for America Program
schemes.ministry: US Department of Agriculture, Rural Development
schemes.tagline: Grants and guaranteed loans for agricultural producers and rural small businesses installing renewable energy systems or improving energy efficiency.
schemes.whatIsThis: REAP funds renewable energy systems (solar, wind, biomass, geothermal, and more) and energy-efficiency improvements for agricultural producers and rural small businesses, expanded significantly by the Inflation Reduction Act.
schemes.objectives: Reduce energy costs and expand renewable energy use in rural America, supporting both climate and rural-economy goals.
eligibility: Agricultural producers (50%+ income from agricultural operations) or rural small businesses.
Project must be in an eligible rural area (for the small-business track).
benefits: Combined grant and guaranteed-loan funding, up to $1,000,000 per applicant.
$200M+ available with roughly 6,000 awards estimated in recent cycles.
Over $2B provided through 2031 under the Inflation Reduction Act expansion.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through your state USDA Rural Development office; funding announcements are published periodically in the Federal Register.

schemes.name: CDFI Fund — Financial & Technical Assistance Awards
schemes.tagline: Treasury funding that builds up Community Development Financial Institutions, which in turn lend to underserved small businesses and founders.
schemes.whatIsThis: The CDFI Fund doesn't lend to startups directly — it certifies and funds Community Development Financial Institutions (banks, credit unions, loan funds, and venture funds with a community-development mission) so they can lend more to underserved communities.
schemes.objectives: Expand economic opportunity for underserved people and communities by growing the capacity of mission-driven community lenders — over 1,300 certified CDFIs nationwide.
eligibility: A startup benefits indirectly by borrowing from or raising from a certified CDFI in its area — not by applying to the CDFI Fund itself.
CDFIs themselves must be certified by Treasury to receive Financial Assistance (FA) or Technical Assistance (TA) awards.
benefits: Grows the pool of mission-driven lenders willing to serve underserved founders and small businesses.
Some certified CDFIs run their own venture-capital funds, not just debt products.
limitations: Not a direct-to-founder program — find a certified CDFI serving your community instead of applying to Treasury.
schemes.howToApply: Search the CDFI Fund's certified-CDFI list for a lender or investor in your area, and apply to that institution directly.
schemes.maxFunding: Indirect — via a certified CDFI lender

schemes.name: New Markets Tax Credit Program
schemes.ministry: US Department of the Treasury (CDFI Fund) / IRS
schemes.tagline: A tax credit that draws private investment into low-income-community businesses through certified Community Development Entities — a founder benefits by being located in a qualifying area.
schemes.whatIsThis: NMTC gives investors a federal tax credit (39% of their investment over 7 years) for equity investments in certified Community Development Entities (CDEs), which then lend to or invest in businesses in low-income communities.
schemes.objectives: Encourage private capital investment in impoverished, low-income communities that otherwise struggle to attract conventional financing.
eligibility: A business benefits by being located in, and getting financing from, a CDE operating in a qualifying low-income census tract.
$10 billion in allocation authority was available for the combined CY2024-2025 round.
benefits: Below-market financing terms are common since CDEs pass along some of the investor tax benefit.
Can fund business loans, real estate, and other qualified low-income community investments.
limitations: A founder can't apply directly to the CDFI Fund — the credit goes to investors and flows through a CDE.
schemes.howToApply: Identify a CDE operating in your low-income census tract and inquire about financing — the CDFI Fund publishes a list of allocatees.

links.label: CDFI Fund — New Markets Tax Credit Program

schemes.howMuch: Indirect — via a CDE in a qualifying tract

schemes.name: GSA Multiple Award Schedule
schemes.tagline: A long-term federal contract vehicle that lets your company sell commercial products/services to any federal, state, or local buyer under pre-negotiated terms — no per-agency bidding required.
schemes.whatIsThis: The MAS program is one of the government's most widely used procurement vehicles. Once on schedule, agencies can order from you directly without a new competitive bid each time, for up to 20 years (5-year base plus three 5-year options).
schemes.objectives: Give commercial companies — 80% of MAS contractors are small businesses — a standing, streamlined path to sell to government buyers.
eligibility: Commercial company offering a product or service the government buys.
Small businesses, including 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, VOSB, and SDVOSB firms, are strongly represented and can be set aside for exclusively.
benefits: No ceiling value; unlimited task/delivery orders under the schedule.
Access to federal, state, local, and tribal buyers through one contract vehicle.
Ordering activities can set aside requirements for eligible small-business categories.
schemes.howToApply: Prepare a GSA Schedule offer (pricing, past performance, compliance documentation) and submit via GSA's eOffer system — an APEX Accelerator can help with this.
schemes.howMuch: N/A — a sales contract vehicle, not funding

schemes.name: USPTO Patent Pro Bono Program
schemes.tagline: Free patent attorney matching for financially under-resourced inventors and small businesses — over $39M in donated legal services since 2015.
schemes.whatIsThis: 20 regional pro bono programs match eligible inventors and small businesses with volunteer patent attorneys and agents to prepare and file patent applications, established under the America Invents Act.
schemes.objectives: Increase access to the patent system for inventors who couldn't otherwise afford a patent attorney, while improving overall patent application quality.
eligibility: Gross household income up to 400% of federal poverty guidelines (e.g., roughly $58,320 for a single person).
Some demonstrated knowledge of the patent system (e.g., a provisional application on file, or a training course).
A genuine invention, not just an idea, and ability to pay standard USPTO filing fees.
benefits: Free attorney/agent time to prepare and prosecute a patent application.
Regional programs may charge a small application fee ($25-$150).
Access to experienced patent practitioners who would otherwise be cost-prohibitive.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through your regional pro bono program (find yours via the USPTO website); you remain responsible for USPTO filing fees.
schemes.howMuch: Free attorney time; standard USPTO fees still due

schemes.name: 8(a) Business Development Program
schemes.tagline: A 9-year program pairing socially and economically disadvantaged business owners with training, technical assistance, and sole-source federal contracting eligibility.
schemes.whatIsThis: 8(a) is structured as a 4-year development stage followed by a 5-year transition stage, designed to build a small business's ability to compete in federal contracting over time rather than just certifying it for set-asides.
schemes.objectives: Help socially and economically disadvantaged small business owners overcome historic barriers to participating in federal contracting.
eligibility: Small business under SBA size standards; at least 51% owned/controlled by a US citizen who is socially and economically disadvantaged.
Personal net worth under $850,000, adjusted gross income under $400,000, assets under $6.5 million.
In business for a demonstrated period showing potential for success; Alaska Native corporations, CDCs, tribes, and Native Hawaiian organizations are also eligible.
Cannot have previously participated in the 8(a) program.
benefits: Sole-source contracts up to $7M (manufacturing) or $4.5M (services).
Structured business-development training and technical assistance throughout the 9-year term.
Access to the SBA's Mentor-Protégé Program.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through SBA's certification portal (certify.sba.gov) after registering in SAM.gov.

schemes.name: HUBZone Program
schemes.tagline: Federal contracting set-asides and a 10% price-evaluation preference for small businesses located in — and employing residents of — historically underutilized business zones.
schemes.whatIsThis: Unlike ownership-based certifications, HUBZone eligibility depends on where your business operates and where your employees live, not who owns the company.
schemes.objectives: Drive job creation and capital investment into distressed communities by channeling federal contracting dollars toward businesses rooted there.
eligibility: Small business under SBA size standards.
At least 51% owned/controlled by US citizens (or a CDC, agricultural cooperative, Alaska Native corporation, Native Hawaiian organization, or Native American tribe).
Principal office located in a HUBZone (check the official map).
At least 35% of employees must be HUBZone residents.
benefits: 10% price-evaluation preference in full-and-open competitions.
Sole-source contracts up to $4.5 million.
HUBZone-restricted set-aside competitions.
schemes.howToApply: Check your address against SBA's HUBZone map, then apply for certification via certify.sba.gov.

schemes.name: Clean Electricity Investment Tax Credit
schemes.tagline: A tax credit worth up to 30%+ of qualifying clean-energy property costs — relevant to any startup building, owning, or hosting solar, storage, or other clean-energy systems.
schemes.whatIsThis: Sections 48 and 48E provide an investment tax credit for a wide range of clean-energy and energy-storage property, with a base rate that multiplies substantially if prevailing-wage/apprenticeship, domestic-content, or energy-community conditions are met.
schemes.objectives: Lower the effective cost of clean-energy investment to accelerate deployment of solar, wind, storage, geothermal, and other qualifying technologies.
eligibility: Ownership of qualifying clean-energy or storage property placed in service in the US.
Base rate is 6%; boosted to 30% by meeting prevailing wage and apprenticeship requirements.
Additional 10-point bonuses available for domestic content and for projects in designated energy communities.
benefits: Dollar-for-dollar reduction in tax liability tied to qualifying investment.
Stackable bonus adders can push the effective credit well above the 30% boosted base rate.
Applies to a broad list of technologies: solar, wind, geothermal, storage, fuel cells, microgrid controllers, and more.
schemes.howToApply: Claim via the applicable IRS form when filing; project-level tax and engineering review is standard given the technical eligibility rules — work with a qualified tax advisor.
schemes.howMuch: 6% base, up to 30%+ with bonus adders

schemes.name: SBA Community Advantage Loan Program
schemes.tagline: A streamlined SBA 7(a)-family loan (up to $250,000) delivered through mission-driven, community-based lenders in underserved areas — often a faster, friendlier path than a bank for a very early business.
schemes.whatIsThis: Community Advantage channels 7(a)-style guaranteed lending through Community Advantage SBLCs — mission-focused, community-based lenders, including Certified Development Companies — rather than traditional banks.
schemes.objectives: Expand access to capital in underserved and rural communities by empowering mission-driven lenders to make smaller SBA-guaranteed loans with lighter paperwork.
eligibility: Startups and existing small businesses in underserved or rural communities.
Apply through a designated Community Advantage lender, not a conventional bank.
benefits: Loans up to $250,000; 85% guarantee below $150,000, 75% above.
Two-page streamlined application; approvals often in 5-10 days.
7-10 year terms for working capital, inventory, acquisitions, or start-up expenses.
schemes.howToApply: Find a Community Advantage SBLC lender through SBA's lender directory — the loan is not applied for directly through SBA.

links.label: SBA — 7(a) loans (Community Advantage is a 7(a) variant)

schemes.name: Manufacturing USA Institutes
schemes.tagline: A network of 16 public-private manufacturing-technology institutes where startups can de-risk new manufacturing processes alongside industry and university partners.
schemes.whatIsThis: Modeled on Germany's Fraunhofer Institutes, each Manufacturing USA institute focuses on a specific advanced-manufacturing technology area, funded through multi-year cooperative agreements between a federal sponsor and a nonfederal operating entity.
schemes.objectives: Bridge the gap between basic research and commercial-scale manufacturing by reducing the cost and risk of adopting new manufacturing processes, and by training the manufacturing workforce.
eligibility: Startups, small manufacturers, and researchers can typically join as institute members or project participants — eligibility and cost vary by institute and technology focus.
Institutes are led by the Departments of Commerce, Defense, or Energy depending on their focus area.
benefits: Access to shared equipment, pilot lines, and technical expertise not affordable to build alone.
Direct connections to industry and university partners solving the same class of manufacturing problem.
Workforce training programs at all skill levels.
schemes.howToApply: Identify the institute matching your technology area on the Manufacturing USA site and contact it directly about membership or project participation.

schemes.name: SBA Surety Bond Guarantee Program
schemes.tagline: SBA guarantees 80-90% of a surety's loss on bid, performance, and payment bonds — letting small contractors bond contracts they couldn't get bonded for commercially.
schemes.whatIsThis: Running since 1971, this program guarantees surety bonds for small businesses that can't obtain them through regular commercial channels, covering contracts up to $9 million ($14 million for certified federal contracts).
schemes.objectives: Increase small businesses' access to federal, state, local, and private-sector contracting that requires bonding.
eligibility: Small business under SBA size standards unable to obtain bonding through normal commercial surety channels.
Applies to contracts up to $9M generally, or $14M with a federal contracting officer's certification of necessity.
benefits: SBA guarantees 80-90% of the surety's loss if the contractor defaults.
In FY2024, SBA guaranteed 11,092 bonds worth $9.21B in total contract value.
Makes sureties willing to bond contractors they'd otherwise decline.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through an SBA-participating surety bond agent/company, not SBA directly.

links.label: SBA — Surety bond partners and agents

schemes.name: Value-Added Producer Grants
schemes.ministry: US Department of Agriculture, Rural Development
schemes.tagline: Grants for agricultural producers turning raw commodities into higher-value products — think berries into jam, or milk into cheese — up to $200,000 for working capital.
schemes.whatIsThis: VAPG funds planning (feasibility studies, business plans) and working capital (processing, packaging, marketing) for agricultural producers moving into value-added products.
schemes.objectives: Generate new products, expand marketing opportunities, and increase producer income by helping farms capture more value from what they grow or raise.
eligibility: Agricultural producers, producer groups, farmer/rancher cooperatives, or majority-controlled producer-based ventures.
Must own and produce more than 50% of the raw commodity and retain greater revenue from the value-added product than from the raw commodity.
Requires a 1:1 matching contribution (cash or eligible in-kind).
benefits: Planning grants up to $50,000; working capital grants up to $200,000.
~$25 million in total funding available in recent cycles.
10% of funds reserved for beginning, veteran, and socially disadvantaged farmers/ranchers plus food-safety projects.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through USDA Rural Development during an open funding cycle; watch for the annual Notice of Funding Opportunity.

links.label: USDA Rural Development — Value-Added Producer Grants

schemes.name: DOD Mentor-Protégé Program
schemes.tagline: Large, experienced DOD contractors formally mentor small businesses to build their capacity as subcontractors and suppliers — made a permanent program in 2023 after 35+ years as a pilot.
schemes.whatIsThis: A large prime contractor (the mentor) enters a formal, DOD-approved agreement to help a small business (the protégé) build technical and business capacity, in exchange for incentives to the mentor.
schemes.objectives: Increase small-business participation and capability in DOD's supply chain, and build durable subcontracting relationships.
eligibility: Protégé must be an eligible small business (including 8(a), HUBZone, WOSB, SDVOSB categories).
Mentor must be an experienced DOD prime contractor entering a mutually developed, DOD-approved agreement.
benefits: Structured technical, managerial, and financial capacity-building from an established prime.
Can lead to real subcontracting work and long-term teaming relationships.
Agency-specific variants exist across DOD components (Navy, Air Force, DTRA, NGA, and more).
schemes.howToApply: Identify a DOD prime willing to mentor you and jointly submit a Mentor-Protégé agreement for DOD approval — often initiated by the mentor.

schemes.name: NSF Regional Innovation Engines
schemes.tagline: Federal awards scaling to up to $160M over 10 years to build an entire regional innovation ecosystem around a shared technology focus — a region-level award, not a single-company grant.
schemes.whatIsThis: NSF Engines funds regional coalitions of industry, academia, government, nonprofits, and community organizations to build innovation ecosystems around a specific technology or industry focus, aiming to make the region a globally competitive hub within about a decade.
schemes.objectives: Close the gap between federally funded research and regional economic growth by funding multi-year, multi-institution partnerships rather than individual companies — the same instinct as the earlier Build to Scale program, at a much larger scale and time horizon.
eligibility: Applicants are multi-institutional regional teams (a lead institution plus partner universities, companies, nonprofits, and local government), not individual startups applying directly.
A founder benefits by joining, partnering with, or being served by an NSF Engine operating in their region and technology area.
NSF Engines Development Awards (Type-1) are a lower-barrier first step for teams not yet ready for a full Engine award.
benefits: Type-1 Development Awards: up to $1M over up to 2 years, to help a region form a team and plan.
Full NSF Engines: start at roughly $15M over the first 2 years, scaling to up to $160M over 10 years for teams that hit milestones.
The first 9 inaugural Engines drew more than $2B in matching commitments from industry, philanthropy, and state/local government.
schemes.howToApply: Individual founders don't apply directly — check NSF's Regional Innovation Engines page for an active Engine in your region and technology area, or join a regional coalition applying for a new one.
schemes.howMuch: ~$15M initial award; up to $160M over 10 years

schemes.name: Regional Technology and Innovation Hubs Program
schemes.ministry: Economic Development Administration (US Dept. of Commerce)
schemes.tagline: CHIPS and Science Act regional grants — $19M to $51M per hub in the first implementation round — designating and funding US regions as globally competitive technology hubs.
schemes.whatIsThis: Tech Hubs is a CHIPS and Science Act program that designates regions positioned to become globally competitive innovation centers within about a decade, then funds a subset of those designated hubs to execute a strategy built around a specific critical technology (semiconductors, biotech, clean energy, and more).
schemes.objectives: Authorized to spend up to $10B over five years (though actual appropriations have been far lower), Tech Hubs aims to spread advanced-technology economic growth beyond existing coastal hubs, strengthening US competitiveness and supply-chain resilience.
eligibility: Applicants are regional consortia (a lead organization plus universities, companies, state/local government, and workforce partners), not individual startups applying directly.
31 regions were designated as official Tech Hubs in October 2023; a subset received Phase 2 implementation funding.
A founder benefits by operating in a designated Tech Hub region and engaging with its consortium's programming.
benefits: Phase 2 implementation awards ranged from about $19M to $51M per hub, totaling roughly $504M across 12 hubs in the first round.
Designated (non-funded) Tech Hubs still gain a federal designation useful for attracting private and state investment.
schemes.howToApply: Individual founders don't apply directly — check EDA's Tech Hubs page for whether your region holds a designation, and connect with that hub's lead consortium organization.

links.label: EDA — Regional Technology and Innovation Hubs

schemes.name: State Small Business Credit Initiative
schemes.tagline: A $10B federal program that capitalizes state-run venture-capital, loan-participation, and collateral-support programs — you apply through your state's specific SSBCI program, not Treasury directly.
schemes.whatIsThis: SSBCI is a Treasury program that allocates federal funds to all 50 states, DC, territories, and participating tribal governments to capitalize their own small-business lending and equity-investment programs, rather than funding companies directly from Washington.
schemes.objectives: Originally created in 2010 and reauthorized and expanded by the American Rescue Plan Act in 2021 with a fresh $10B, SSBCI aims to unlock private lending and investment for small businesses that traditional credit markets underserve, with jurisdictions expected to leverage each federal dollar into roughly $10 of private financing.
eligibility: Eligibility depends entirely on the specific program your state built with its SSBCI allocation — a venture-capital co-investment fund, loan-participation program, loan-guarantee program, or collateral-support program.
Most SSBCI-funded programs target small businesses and startups that can show a private lender or investor already willing to participate alongside the state.
States are required to dedicate a portion of funds to very small businesses (fewer than 10 employees) and underserved entrepreneurs.
benefits: Access to state-run venture funds, loan guarantees, or collateral support that make a private lender or investor's deal possible.
Program terms (loan size, equity check size, guarantee percentage) vary widely by state — check your state's specific SSBCI program page.
schemes.howToApply: Find your state's SSBCI-capitalized program through your state's economic development or treasury agency — Treasury's SSBCI page links to each participating jurisdiction's program page.

links.label: US Treasury — State Small Business Credit Initiative

schemes.howMuch: Varies by state program (loan, guarantee, or equity co-investment)

schemes.name: State Trade Expansion Program
schemes.tagline: SBA grants to states — $100,000 to $900,000 per award — that fund export assistance for small businesses, from trade-show travel to website globalization.
schemes.whatIsThis: STEP is an SBA grant program that funds individual states to help their small businesses start or expand exporting, running since 2011. States use the grant to reimburse small-business exporters for specific eligible costs.
schemes.objectives: Increase the number of small businesses exporting, increase the dollar value of small-business exports, and help small businesses explore significant new international trade opportunities.
eligibility: Small business as defined by SBA size standards, already exporting or actively pursuing export opportunities.
Apply through your state's STEP program administrator — eligible activities and reimbursement amounts vary by state.
benefits: Reimbursement for costs like trade-show participation, trade-mission travel, export training, translated marketing materials, and website globalization/e-commerce.
FY2026 state awards ranged from $100,000 to $900,000, with SBA anticipating about $20M in total awards nationally.
schemes.howToApply: Find your state's STEP program (usually run by the state's international trade or commerce office) and apply through that state's specific application cycle and rules.
schemes.maxFunding: Varies by state (state awards up to $900,000 total)

schemes.name: Boots to Business
schemes.tagline: Free entrepreneurship training for transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses, delivered on military installations worldwide and online.
schemes.whatIsThis: Boots to Business is an entrepreneurial education program SBA runs as part of the Department of Defense's Transition Assistance Program, teaching the fundamentals of business ownership to people leaving military service.
schemes.objectives: Give transitioning service members and military spouses a structured, no-cost introduction to entrepreneurship and startup capital resources as one option for their post-service career.
eligibility: Active-duty service members (including National Guard and Reserve) within the Transition Assistance Program window.
Boots to Business Reboot extends the same curriculum to veterans of any era in their local community.
Military spouses are eligible for both formats; there is no cost to participants.
benefits: In-person or virtual training on business fundamentals, delivered on 195+ military installations worldwide.
Boots to Business Revenue Readiness: a 6-week online program turning an idea into an actual business model.
Graduates can continue into an 8-week advanced online course through partners like Syracuse University's Institute for Veterans and Military Families, covering grant proposals and business planning.
schemes.howToApply: Sign up through your installation's Transition Assistance Program office (active duty) or via SBA's Boots to Business page (Reboot, for veterans in the community).

schemes.name: T.H.R.I.V.E. Emerging Leaders Reimagined
schemes.tagline: A free, 6-month executive growth program for established small businesses with at least $250,000 in revenue — built for scaling an existing business, not a pre-revenue startup.
schemes.whatIsThis: SBA THRIVE (successor to the Emerging Leaders initiative launched in 2008-09) is an executive-level training series pairing established small-business owners with professional coaches and mentors to build a concrete growth plan.
schemes.objectives: Accelerate the growth of high-potential small businesses, particularly in historically underserved communities, by developing owners' strategic and leadership capacity rather than handing out capital.
eligibility: Business must have at least $250,000 in annual revenue.
Must have been operating for at least 3 years.
Must have at least one employee besides the owner.
benefits: In-person and self-paced instruction, mentoring, and classroom time over roughly 6 months, at no cost.
Participants produce a 3-year strategic growth action plan with concrete benchmarks.
Access to a peer cohort, local business leaders, and the local financial community.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through SBA's THRIVE program page or a local SBA district office running a cohort in your area.

schemes.name: Empower to Grow (7(j) Management and Technical Assistance Program)
schemes.tagline: Free business courses, tailored training, and one-on-one consulting for small businesses in underserved areas or federal contracting certifications, aimed at winning government contracts.
schemes.whatIsThis: Empower to Grow (formerly the 7(j) Management and Technical Assistance Program, authorized under Section 7(j) of the Small Business Act) funds private-sector service providers to deliver management and technical assistance to eligible small businesses.
schemes.objectives: Build the operational, financial, and government-contracting capacity of small businesses that face structural barriers to accessing capital and federal contracts.
eligibility: Located in an area of high unemployment or low income, OR
Owned by low-income individuals, OR
Certified as an 8(a), HUBZone, or Economically Disadvantaged Women-Owned Small Business (EDWOSB) participant.
benefits: Free counseling and training in financing, accounting, marketing, and operations.
Help identifying and developing new business opportunities, including federal contracting bids.
In FY2023, participating firms averaged a self-reported 45% growth in annual revenue, with a 60% win rate on federal contract bids submitted.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through SBA's Empower to Grow / 7(j) program page, which connects eligible businesses to an approved service provider.
schemes.maxFunding: N/A — free training and consulting, not funding

schemes.name: NSF Convergence Accelerator
schemes.tagline: Multi-phase NSF funding for multidisciplinary teams tackling national-scale challenges, moving from proof-of-concept toward real-world deployment.
schemes.whatIsThis: Launched in 2019, the Convergence Accelerator funds teams that combine research disciplines, sectors, and organization types to accelerate solutions to challenges too broad for any single field, organized into annual thematic tracks (cohorts).
schemes.objectives: Bridge the gap between basic NSF-funded research and real-world, national-scale impact by funding structured, cohort-based teams through a two-phase process: proof-of-concept, then scaling and transition to practice.
eligibility: Universities, nonprofits, tribal organizations, for-profit companies (including qualified small businesses), and national labs can participate.
Teams typically form around a specific year's announced thematic track.
Phase 1 supports team formation, user discovery, and proof-of-concept; Phase 2 supports full development, prototyping, and scaling.
benefits: Phase 1 funding for planning and proof-of-concept development.
Phase 2 funding for full solution development and scaling into practice.
Structured cohort model gives teams facilitated collaboration and mentorship alongside the funding.
schemes.howToApply: Watch for NSF's annual Convergence Accelerator solicitation announcing that year's thematic tracks, and apply as part of a multidisciplinary team through NSF's proposal process.
schemes.howMuch: Varies by track and phase (Phase 1 + Phase 2)

schemes.name: Women's Business Centers
schemes.tagline: A nationwide network of roughly 100 SBA-backed centers giving women entrepreneurs free or low-cost training, counseling, and access to SBA's full financing and procurement toolkit.
schemes.whatIsThis: WBCs are SBA resource-partner centers, established in 1988, that provide business training and counseling to entrepreneurs — particularly women who are economically or socially disadvantaged — in finance, management, marketing, and technology.
schemes.objectives: Help women overcome persistent barriers to starting and growing small businesses by pairing free or low-cost training with direct access to SBA lending and contracting programs.
eligibility: Open to any aspiring or existing entrepreneur (the network is chartered to prioritize women, but services are broadly available).
No cost or nominal cost for most services.
About 100 centers nationwide plus territories, each independently run by a host nonprofit or institution.
benefits: Free or low-cost training in finance, marketing, and management, often in multiple languages.
Direct referral into SBA loan and federal-contracting programs.
Businesses assisted by a WBC show meaningfully better survival rates than the overall small-business population.
schemes.howToApply: Find your nearest center via SBA's Office of Women's Business Ownership locator and contact it directly — there is no separate national application.
schemes.maxFunding: N/A — free or low-cost training and counseling

schemes.name: SCORE Mentors
schemes.tagline: Free, lifelong access to 10,000+ volunteer business mentors nationwide — SBA's largest resource-partner network, with no revenue or stage requirement to qualify.
schemes.whatIsThis: SCORE is a nonprofit SBA resource partner, founded in 1964, that matches entrepreneurs at any stage with experienced volunteer mentors for one-on-one advice by phone, video, or email, alongside free workshops and templates.
schemes.objectives: Increase small-business formation and survival by removing cost as a barrier to experienced business mentorship.
eligibility: Open to anyone starting, running, or exiting a small business — no revenue, stage, or industry restriction.
benefits: Free, ongoing one-on-one mentoring matched to your industry or challenge.
Free local and online workshops, templates, and business-planning tools.
11 million+ entrepreneurs assisted since founding.
schemes.howToApply: Request a mentor through SCORE's website; matches are typically made within a few days.

schemes.name: Veterans Business Outreach Center
schemes.tagline: A 31-location network of SBA-funded counseling centers giving transitioning service members, veterans, and military spouses free entrepreneurial training, mentoring, and contracting guidance.
schemes.whatIsThis: VBOCs are SBA resource partners dedicated to the military community, running workshops, one-on-one counseling, and business-plan support, and serving as the delivery mechanism for Boots to Business in many locations.
schemes.objectives: Give the military community — active duty transitioning out, veterans of any era, Guard/Reserve, and military spouses — a dedicated, no-cost entry point into SBA's full range of programs.
eligibility: Service members (including National Guard and Reserve), veterans, and military spouses/family members.
benefits: No-cost workshops, training, and one-on-one mentoring.
Government-contracting guidance specific to veteran-owned businesses.
Referral into SBA's broader lender and resource-partner network.
schemes.howToApply: Use SBA's VBOC locator to find and contact your nearest of 31 centers nationwide.

schemes.name: Women-Owned Small Business Federal Contracting Program
schemes.tagline: Set-aside and sole-source federal contracts reserved for certified women-owned small businesses, working toward the government's 5%-of-contract-dollars goal.
schemes.whatIsThis: The WOSB Program lets federal contracting officers set aside — or in some cases sole-source — contracts in industries where SBA has determined women-owned businesses are underrepresented or substantially underrepresented.
schemes.objectives: Give certified WOSBs (and Economically Disadvantaged WOSBs, EDWOSBs) fairer access to federal procurement in specific NAICS-coded industries.
eligibility: At least 51% owned and controlled by women who are US citizens.
Women manage day-to-day operations and make long-term decisions.
Must be a small business under SBA size standards for the relevant NAICS code.
Must be in an industry SBA has designated as underrepresented (WOSB) or substantially underrepresented (EDWOSB) for set-asides.
benefits: Access to contracts set aside exclusively for certified WOSBs/EDWOSBs.
EDWOSBs are additionally eligible for sole-source awards in qualifying industries.
Certification is done directly through SBA at no cost.
schemes.howToApply: Certify through SBA's WOSB Program portal — self-certification has been phased out, so certification now runs through SBA or an approved third-party certifier.

links.label: SBA — Women-Owned Small Business Federal Contracting Program

schemes.maxFunding: N/A — contracting eligibility, not direct funding

schemes.name: Veteran-Owned & Service-Disabled Veteran-Owned Small Business Contracting
schemes.tagline: Federal set-aside and sole-source contracts reserved for certified veteran-owned and service-disabled veteran-owned small businesses.
schemes.whatIsThis: Parallel to the WOSB Program, this lets contracting officers set aside — or sole-source — contracts for VOSBs and SDVOSBs. Certification authority moved from the VA to SBA's Veteran Small Business Certification (VetCert) process starting January 2023 under the FY2021 NDAA.
schemes.objectives: Ensure veteran-owned and service-disabled-veteran-owned small businesses can compete for a dedicated share of federal contracting dollars.
eligibility: At least 51% owned and controlled by one or more veterans (VOSB) or service-disabled veterans (SDVOSB).
Must be a small business under SBA size standards.
Self-certification is no longer accepted — formal SBA certification is required.
benefits: Access to VOSB/SDVOSB set-aside contracts government-wide.
SDVOSBs are additionally eligible for sole-source awards in qualifying situations.
VA-specific contracts have their own parallel verification track.
limitations: Certification rules changed in 2023 and remain in flux — verify current VetCert/Dynamic Small Business Search requirements directly with SBA before relying on this program.
schemes.howToApply: Apply for certification through SBA's Veteran Small Business Certification program; confirm current requirements before applying, since verification rules have changed recently.
schemes.maxFunding: N/A — contracting eligibility, not direct funding

schemes.name: SBA Export Express Loan
schemes.tagline: SBA's fastest export loan — up to $500,000 with a 90% guarantee and lender approval in as little as 36 hours.
schemes.whatIsThis: Export Express lets participating lenders use their own underwriting to approve a loan for export-related purposes, backed by an SBA guarantee, without needing SBA's prior sign-off on each loan.
schemes.objectives: Speed up small exporters' access to capital by letting trusted lenders self-approve within SBA guidelines rather than going through standard 7(a) review.
eligibility: Small business under SBA size standards.
In operation at least 12 months.
Must show the loan will help enter a new export market or expand an existing one.
benefits: Loans up to $500,000.
SBA guarantees up to 90% of the loan.
Approval from participating lenders in as little as 36 hours.
Funds usable for export transactions, working capital, marketing, or equipment.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through an SBA-participating Export Express lender — find one via SBA's lender match tool or your local SBA Office of International Trade.

schemes.name: SBA International Trade Loan
schemes.tagline: SBA-guaranteed term loans up to $5 million — a guarantee as high as 90% for small manufacturers — for businesses expanding exports or facing import competition.
schemes.whatIsThis: A 7(a) loan variant specifically for businesses developing new export markets, expanding existing ones, or needing to modernize to compete against imports, with a higher SBA guarantee than a standard 7(a) loan.
schemes.objectives: Improve the competitive position of small exporters and import-affected businesses through larger, longer-term guaranteed financing than Export Express offers.
eligibility: Small business under SBA size standards.
Loan proceeds must support export expansion or competitiveness against import competition.
Terms up to 25 years depending on use of funds.
benefits: Loans up to $5 million.
Guarantee up to 90% for small manufacturers (up from the standard 75%).
Usable for facilities, equipment, working capital, debt refinance, or business acquisition tied to trade competitiveness.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through an SBA-participating 7(a) lender, submitting SBA Form 4 and required exhibits.
schemes.howMuch: Up to $5M (up to 90% guarantee for manufacturers)

schemes.name: EXIM Global Credit Express
schemes.ministry: Export-Import Bank of the United States
schemes.tagline: A revolving line of credit up to $500,000 for small exporters, financing the business of exporting itself rather than a single transaction.
schemes.whatIsThis: Global Credit Express (GCE) is EXIM's short-term working-capital product for small exporters, delivered through a select network of participating lenders, distinct from EXIM's transaction-specific Working Capital Guarantee Program.
schemes.objectives: Give small exporters liquidity to run and grow their export business generally, not just to finance one deal, filling a gap private lenders often won't.
eligibility: Small business per SBA size standards with export sales history or firm export orders.
Must apply through one of EXIM's designated GCE participating lenders.
benefits: Revolving credit line up to $500,000.
6-12 month terms.
Financing tied to the exporter's overall business, not one transaction.
schemes.howToApply: Apply through one of EXIM's participating GCE lenders — check EXIM's website for the current lender list.

schemes.name: US International Development Finance Corporation Financing
schemes.tagline: Loans, loan guarantees, political-risk insurance, and equity for US companies — including startups — operating in emerging and developing markets.
schemes.whatIsThis: DFC, formed in 2019 from OPIC and USAID's Development Credit Authority, provides debt and equity financing to private-sector projects in developing countries, with a mandate that includes supporting small and women-led businesses.
schemes.objectives: Mobilize private capital toward development challenges abroad (energy, health, infrastructure, technology) while advancing US foreign-policy and commercial interests.
eligibility: US-connected businesses (majority US ownership, or significant US benefit) with a project or operations in an eligible developing country.
Project must meet DFC's development-impact and additionality criteria.
benefits: Debt financing, loan guarantees, and equity investment for qualifying projects.
Political-risk insurance for US investors abroad.
Technical assistance alongside financing in some programs.
schemes.howToApply: Submit a project proposal through DFC's online application portal at dfc.gov.
schemes.howMuch: Varies by project (debt, guarantee, or equity)

schemes.name: US Trade and Development Agency Project Preparation Funding
schemes.tagline: Grants — typically around $500,000 — that fund feasibility studies and technical assistance connecting US companies to infrastructure projects in emerging markets.
schemes.whatIsThis: USTDA funds feasibility studies, technical assistance, and pilot projects that help emerging-market infrastructure projects move toward financing while integrating US goods, services, and expertise.
schemes.objectives: Advance overseas economic development while promoting US exports, by de-risking early project-preparation work that draws in US firms.
eligibility: US companies providing goods, services, or expertise relevant to a specific overseas infrastructure project.
Typically initiated in partnership with the host-country project sponsor requesting USTDA support.
benefits: Grants typically around $500,000, rarely exceeding $1 million.
Funds feasibility studies, technical assistance, and pilot projects.
Studies help host countries and lenders assess project viability, often leading to procurement of US goods and services.
schemes.howToApply: Host-country project sponsors (often with a US company partner) submit funding requests directly to USTDA.

schemes.name: DOE Loan Programs Office — Title 17 Clean Energy Financing
schemes.tagline: Federal loan guarantees for clean-energy and energy-infrastructure projects, ranging from partial commercial-loan guarantees to full guarantees on Federal Financing Bank loans.
schemes.whatIsThis: LPO's Title 17 program finances later-stage clean-energy, supply-chain, and energy-infrastructure-reinvestment projects that are ready for commercial deployment but still face a financing gap, through loan guarantees rather than grants.
schemes.objectives: Deploy clean energy and reduce emissions by guaranteeing debt for capital-intensive projects private lenders won't fully finance alone — a deployment tool, not an early-stage R&D program.
eligibility: Project-based, not company-based — must fall into the Innovative Energy, Innovative Supply Chain, State Energy Financing Institution-Supported, or Energy Infrastructure Reinvestment categories.
Non-competitive but rigorous, ongoing application process (not a single annual deadline).
benefits: Guarantees up to 100% of Federal Financing Bank loans.
Partial guarantees up to 90% of commercial lender loans.
No cap comparable to a typical grant program — sized to the project.
schemes.howToApply: Submit a Part I application directly to LPO through its ongoing, non-competitive intake process at energy.gov/lpo.

schemes.name: BARDA DRIVe
schemes.ministry: Department of Health and Human Services (BARDA)
schemes.tagline: Non-dilutive and equity-style funding plus accelerator support for health-security innovations — from diagnostics to sepsis to pandemic preparedness — outside BARDA's traditional medical-countermeasure pipeline.
schemes.whatIsThis: DRIVe (Division of Research, Innovation, and Ventures) uses BARDA's 21st Century Cures Act authorities to fund novel approaches to systemic health-security problems, combining proof-of-concept funding with an accelerator network that finds promising startups nationwide.
schemes.objectives: Solve health-security challenges that cut across specific diseases (like early sepsis detection or platform diagnostics) by funding outside BARDA's usual product-specific model.
eligibility: Startups and small companies working on health-security-relevant technology.
DRIVe funding opportunities are announced by specific topic area rather than a single standing solicitation.
Some engagement happens via the DRIVe Accelerator Network's regional scouts.
benefits: Proof-of-concept and R&D funding, both non-dilutive and dilutive depending on the mechanism.
Access to the DRIVe Accelerator Network's mentorship and industry connections.
Path to larger BARDA procurement/contracting for successful technologies.
schemes.howToApply: Monitor DRIVe's open solicitations at drive.hhs.gov or connect through a DRIVe Accelerator Network partner in your region.

schemes.name: DHS Silicon Valley Innovation Program
schemes.ministry: Department of Homeland Security (Science and Technology Directorate)
schemes.tagline: Up to $800,000 in non-dilutive funding across four fast phases, using a streamlined Other Transaction Authority process built to move at startup speed.
schemes.whatIsThis: SVIP funds startups solving specific homeland-security technology problems (published as topic calls), using DHS's Other Transaction Authority to award and pay out funding far faster than a typical federal contract.
schemes.objectives: Get startups' emerging technology into DHS's hands quickly, reshaping how government and startups collaborate, rather than relying solely on traditional large-contractor procurement.
eligibility: Fewer than 200 employees.
No more than $1 million in prior 12-month government contracts.
Must respond to a specific, published SVIP topic call.
benefits: Non-dilutive funding across 3-4 phases at $50,000-$200,000 per phase, up to $800,000 total.
Awards typically finalized in about 45 days via Other Transaction Solicitations.
Direct engagement with DHS operational components as potential customers.
schemes.howToApply: Watch for open topic calls on SVIP's portal and submit a solution brief in response to a specific call.

schemes.name: MBDA Capital Readiness Program
schemes.ministry: Minority Business Development Agency (US Dept. of Commerce)
schemes.tagline: A $125M program funding accelerators and incubators that prepare minority and other underserved entrepreneurs to raise capital from SSBCI and beyond.
schemes.whatIsThis: The largest federal program of its kind, CRP funds organizations to run capacity-building programs — training, pitch development, investor connections — that help underserved founders become investable, complementing the state-run SSBCI capital itself.
